title: Toward Reconfigurable In-Pixel Computing: A Fault-Tolerant Design Flow for Machine Learning Accelerators: (Invited Paper)
problem: Current HLS-generated hardware designs for in-pixel computing lack flexibility for task adaptation and robustness against single-event upsets (SEUs) in radiation environments. Existing implementations cannot be reconfigured post-deployment or efficiently handle fault tolerance constraints.
motivation: In-pixel computing enables low-latency real-time machine learning inference directly on sensors for edge applications, but only if hardware can be both adaptable and resilient.
method: A fault-tolerant framework performs bit-level vulnerability analysis on neural network weights to identify critical components, then selectively applies Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) to those components. Custom memory modules are integrated into the HLS workflow to enable post-deployment reconfiguration. A TMR-aware back-end synthesis flow dynamically allocates redundancy according to user-defined area and power constraints.
key_novelty: Selective bit-level vulnerability-aware TMR allocation that enables simultaneous post-deployment reconfiguration and adaptive fault tolerance within an HLS-integrated design flow.
contributions: Framework for bit-level vulnerability analysis of neural network weights to identify fault-critical regions
Selective Triple Modular Redundancy mechanism that adapts redundancy to area and power budgets
Integration of custom memory modules into HLS workflow for post-deployment task reconfiguration
TMR-aware back-end synthesis flow with dynamic redundancy allocation

metrics.area: scalable implementations mentioned but no concrete numbers
metrics.power: constrained via dynamic allocation but no concrete numbers

limitations: Specific quantitative results, comparison baselines, and actual workload performance metrics are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Adaptive fault-tolerant reconfigurable hardware for in-pixel machine learning
